name: Low-cost 3D-printed self-driving lab for reaction optimisation (2026)
brief: A self-driving lab for optimising organic reaction conditions: pumps dose reagents into a reactor, a liquid sample collector takes aliquots, and an existing in-house analytical instrument (HPLC, NMR or Raman) measures yield in a closed loop. One fume hood, academic budget.

cost.original: $5000, a 90% reduction on the team's earlier $50,000 version
cost.excludes_note: Analytical instruments are not included in the reported figure.
